title: Tenant throttle sandbox, predictive reservation model, and bounded burst policy rework
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: During a weekday morning capacity event we observed a single tenant’s traffic pattern triggering sustained KV-cache pressure and prolonged GPU reservation exhaustion on two Dedicated clusters. The immediate effects were elevated tail latency for colocated tenants, several hard evictions, and a temporary increase in cost due to emergency burst allocations. Root cause hypothesis: combination of under-provisioned reservation sizing for that tenant’s workload (p95 > reserved capacity), an unbounded burst policy that allowed sustained bursts beyond the intended short window, and insufficient noisy-neighbor isolation (tenant processes shared cgroups with lax limits). Decision: build a repeatable tenant-throttle sandbox for controlled experiments, replace the static reservation-sizing heuristic with a short-term predictive model based on p95/p99 usage and drift, and implement a bounded burst token model with decay and a soft-eviction fallback path.
acceptance_criteria: Repeatable sandbox reproduces the incident signature (KV cache pressure + sustained reservation saturation) within 3 run iterations
New predictive reservation model keeps hard evictions for similar workloads to <=1% of baseline over 2-week simulated runs
Burst policy is updated to a token-bucket with 60s decay window and default cap that prevents hour-scale sustained bursts
New tenant isolation knobs (per-tenant cgroup soft limits + leak-bucket) are available behind a flag and documented
Dashboards and alerting: cluster-level eviction rate, tenant-level burst tokens, and predictive headroom estimates are added to Console
